knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The source lists soil type, surface, water quality, method and cost as the basis for choice. Price alone is not enough.
The source warns that trace detergent on food can make people unwell, with symptoms resembling food poisoning, so the rinse has to be complete.
Parts such as saw bands, pipes and stuffers are taken apart so the cleaning action reaches soil that would otherwise be hidden.
The apply, allow dwell time and agitate section says foam is applied and left for several minutes before rinsing.

practicalCriteria: Learner selects a detergent for a named soil and surface and states the reason (pass: soil, surface, water and method all named).
Observer confirms the dwell time is timed and the surface is agitated where needed (pass: timer used and agitation recorded).
Observer checks the final rinse for foam or detergent (pass: none visible, or rinse repeated).
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Product selection note with label and SDS references
Observer checklist for dwell time and rinse
Record of dilution and dwell time
stopWorkCriteria: Two products are about to be mixed, or a product has been poured into an unlabelled container.
The label or SDS is missing or unreadable.
Foam or residue remains after the rinse and the rinse cannot be repeated.
Wastewater would enter a drain that the site has not approved for it.
